project: Engenharia Reversa — original REA Linux VPS
purpose: Apply the existing P232 binary-session hold to every live tools/call using the existing GitHub Actions transport; preserve owner verification, service, original REA code and six P214 Evidence.

before.problem: P232 was only optional pre-sealing operator guard. Existing sealed_batch executed open_binary and automatically closed it in finally, or legacy source-owned fixtures could reach open_binary/close_binary. Previous P225 close_binary wiped global Evidence/Unknown state.

defense_in_depth: p232_guard_live_call called at beginning of central request_mcp before constructing urllib HTTP request; affects all original-MCP call sources including historic source-owned fixtures and automatic close_binary cleanup.

p232_guard_inner_batch called AFTER original secure.validate_inner / Ed25519 checks but BEFORE one-use nonce claim and before first step: rejects whole mixed batches atomically without consuming nonce.
Malformed tools/call name/params and malformed inner steps fail closed.
Harmless initialize, tools/list and other authorized queries are unaffected.
Existing per-tool workspace authorizations and owner-sensitive signatures remain mandatory; this guard can only remove permission, never grant it.
Original P232 local operator preseal guard remains unchanged and required.
Guard is in the preexisting bridge only; does not install a new plugin, skill, MCP, engine or server.

test_evidence.native_execution_scope: Existing Python bridge loaded via stdin on original Linux VPS, zero unit-test calls to real binary lifecycle tools
test_evidence.earlier_diagnostic_note: First test harness attempted to import bridge through filesystem path. The original bridge runs via stdin. This failed before tests started; corrected by executing 17 tests against the already-loaded bridge in memory.

limitations: The guard is enforced in the GitHub/Skill transport's central live request_mcp, not inside the original REA MCP service; independent local clients to 127.0.0.1:8765 may bypass it.
It intentionally prevents open_binary/close_binary even with fresh owner signature until a separate independently approved safe lifecycle release.
Other sensitive tools that implicitly retire an active provider may still need independent review; do not assume all 83 sensitive tools are safe.
No live binary close/restart was attempted, so permanent Evidence durability after actual daemon restart remains unproven.
No new per-tool functional certification occurred, total remains 116/208.
This commit intentionally updates bridge source from the previous original SHA; workflow and signing policy are unchanged.
